text.text: Numbers from seanome/2024-kmerseek-analysis at commit 4a4b1171 (results/leaderboard), copied 2026-10-15.
Tool id hmmscan. Numbers from seanome/2024-kmerseek-analysis commit 4a4b1171.
Each query protein against the curated profile models of every Pfam family, without searching any relative.
Domain bit score: higher ranks first. E-value cutoffs 10 (sequence and domain).

Under the Pfam truth set, raw calls, no relative (hmmscan searches the Pfam models), its best setting is direct: Fmax 0.886 over 2,435 true instances. Below, each stratum compares this setting with the best setting of any other tool in that same stratum, so the other tool's setting can change from line to line. Only strata with at least 30 true instances are compared.
No other tool was scored in the same strata, so no comparison: not run.

Pfam domains are defined by these same models, so scoring hmmscan against the Pfam truth set grades the models against their own output. Read its Pfam row as the best a search could do, not as a competitor.
It was scored against the Pfam truth set only. Swiss-Prot features and Pfam-N: not run.

Setting direct, scanning Pfam's models: 0.389 core-hours reserved per 1,000 queries (4 cores for the task's wall time), measured on Sherlock. Peak memory 0.5 GB. That is about $0.0173 at $0.044625 per CPU-hour. Building its databases: not measured.
The per-query cost counts the search only. The run recorded cost per tool and setting, summed over all relatives, so the cost for one relative is the mean.

Hardware of the search (setting direct, every task): Sherlock partition hns, from the trace. Host name: not recorded in the trace, so the node is the one SLURM's job record (sacct) gives. 1 task on 1 node. CPU: AMD 9754 (1 task). GPU: none allocated.
Hardware of the database build: not recorded, since the run's task records hold no such task.

Sources, read 2026-10-16: the partition is the queue column of the run's Nextflow traces. The traces have no hostname column, so the node is the one SLURM's job record (sacct) gives for the trace's job id. CPU and GPU are that node's features in SLURM (scontrol show node: CPU_MNF, CPU_SKU, GPU_SKU), named as on Sherlock's node features page. Partition hns is owned by a research group, and Sherlock's tech specs page lists no CPU models for such partitions. Script: scripts/read_hardware.py.
Licence: BSD 3-clause (HMMER); CC0 1.0 (Pfam-A models, per the Pfam 38.2 release notes) (source)
direct: scans Pfam's models; no relative searched
Is every family you expect to find already in Pfam? If no, this tool cannot find it: it only reports families that have a Pfam model.

Are the features you care about longer than 60 residues? If yes, Fmax here is 61–120 aa 0.785 (n = 963), 121–250 aa 0.802 (n = 504), 251 aa or more 0.871 (n = 277). If no, 16–30 aa 0.580 (n = 271), 31–60 aa 0.573 (n = 420). (Pfam truth set, raw calls, no relative searched, setting direct.)
Can you spend about 0.389 core-hours per 1,000 proteins? That is the measured cost of scanning them against Pfam's models.
